newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU committee did not discuss punt, officials say.
newsitem.headline: EU committee did not discuss punt, officials say.

text.p: The European Union's monetary committee ended a meeting on Friday without discussing the strengthening Irish punt, committee sources said.
"We have discussed (the items that were) on the agenda," one official said. The punt was not on the agenda.
Asked whether the Irish currency had been raised, another official said, "No".

The secretive committee of national treasury and central bank officials met amid market speculation of a possible revaluation of the punt, but EU officials said it would focus on a number of issues pertaining to economic and monetary union (EMU).

EU monetary officials on Wednesday said the Irish economy's fundamentals did not justify a revaluation of the punt. "There is no intention whatsoever to talk about the Irish punt," a senior EU official told Reuters.
Instead the meeting was due to discuss various EMU-related issues including relations between EU finance ministers and a future European Central Bank.
It was also slated to discuss the relationship between the euro and currencies such as the dollar and EMU's impact on the International Monetary Fund.
Another point on the agenda was how the monetary committee will eventually evolve into the so-called Economic and Financial Committee after the euro is launched.
